the old rats, but not the young rats, were able to tolerate a greater amount of myocardial damage and infarction after exercise.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exercise is beneficial to the aging heart, and that the aging heart is more sensitive to the beneficial effect of exercise than the young heart.
exercise improves the cardiac performance of old rats, and this effect is due, at least in part, to a reduction in myocardial ischemia.
, in young rats, exercise did not improve survival, and the ECG tracines did not show a difference between exercise and sedentary animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
regular exercise can improve cardiac function and reduce cardiac damage in older animals, but it has no effect on young rats.
exercise can be beneficial to the aging heart, even in the face of a major stressor like myocardial infarct.
exercise is an important factor for maintaining cardiac health in old rats.
